We want to understand what you meant by "there was something near the bottom of the screen, some kind of action I think, though I couldn't quite tell what it was for", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The large “Continue Shopping” bar placed near the bottom, which appears more visually prominent than the order-related control below it.

B) The lighter “Place Order” bar underneath “Continue Shopping,” which is present but visually de-emphasized in the lower section.

C) The small terms and privacy policy text at the very bottom, which sits below the action area and may make the purpose of the lower section less clear.

D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
turns.a: If I had to pick... probably B? I think. Though I'm not sure that's exactly it — it might be closer to another option, depending on how you're defining it. It's more of a general feeling than a specific thing. Other people might not even notice.

turns.q: What kind of ordering situation would bring you to a layout where “Continue Shopping” is prominent but “Place Order” appears lighter underneath?
turns.a: I'm not sure I have one specific moment in mind. It's more of a... recurring thing, I suppose. When the team needs to process something quickly and there's not much time for setup. Though I'm not sure that's specific enough.

turns.q: When you noticed the lighter “Place Order” bar beneath “Continue Shopping,” what were you trying to confirm about the ordering options shown in that lower section?
turns.a: I suppose just... complete the transaction. Get it submitted. I don't usually think of it as a 'job' — it's more like a step in something larger. Someone else usually handles the follow-up.

turns.q: What would the lower section need to communicate visually so “Place Order” feels like the clear next step rather than secondary to “Continue Shopping”?
turns.a: I mean... it was just a small thing. The button wasn't as prominent as I expected. Most of the time I'd figure it out. It's not a blocker, exactly.

turns.q: If the lighter “Place Order” bar were shown exactly right, what visual treatment would make it feel like the main action in that lower section?
turns.a: The problem is visibility, really. The button to submit — the 'Place Order' button — didn't look like a primary action. It looked like a label. So I spent time looking for something that was already there, just... not visible enough.

turns.q: In the lower section, what visible cue would tell you at a glance that “Place Order” is the final checkout action?
turns.a: The button was gray on a gray background with very small text — 12 pixels, I think. For the primary action on the screen, that's basically invisible. I couldn't tell if it was meant to be interactive, if it was disabled, or if I was just overlooking it. The barrier is the contrast. To remove it: give the 'Place Order' button a solid fill color that actually stands out from the background, and increase the text to something legible — 16 pixels minimum. That's the change. Everything else on the screen was fine.

turns.q: On the “Place Order” bar, is the problem mainly that it has no solid fill, that the color is too light, or that the contrast against the background is too low?
turns.a: "A filled button — solid color background, not gray, not a ghost outline. White text on a brand color, or dark text on a light fill — whatever gives you readable contrast. Something that registers immediately as 'this is interactive, this is what I press.' Right now it doesn't register as that at all. That's the only fix needed."
